name: Congenital Partial Agenesis of Pericardium

criteria.description: Demonstration of partial absence of the pericardium on imaging modalities such as cardiac MRI or CT
Electrocardiogram showing right axis deviation, incomplete right bundle branch block, or other nonspecific changes
Symptoms such as atypical chest pain or positional dyspnea consistent with partial pericardial agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of partial pericardial absence is required; clinical and ECG findings support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often incidental during imaging for other indications; no standardized diagnostic criteria exist

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intermittent positional chest pain due to cardiac displacement
searchTerms: positional chest discomfort from heart shift

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac efficiency
searchTerms: fatigue due to poor heart pumping
heart beat felt more to the side
strong heart impulse felt away from center

occasional.symptomName: Murmur due to altered cardiac motion
searchTerms: heart murmur from abnormal heart motion
murmur caused by altered cardiac movement
abnormal heart sounds due to motion
getting tired easily with physical activity

rare.symptomName: Sudden cardiac arrest due to cardiac herniation
searchTerms: sudden heart stoppage from heart displacement
cardiac arrest caused by heart herniation
unexpected cardiac arrest due to heart shift

imaging: Cardiac MRI showing absence of pericardial tissue over left or right heart border
CT scan demonstrating partial pericardial defect
Chest X-ray showing leftward displacement of cardiac silhouette
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Electrocardiogram with right axis deviation or incomplete right bundle branch block

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of pericardium on imaging
Usually asymptomatic or less symptomatic than partial agenesis
Fluid accumulation around the heart on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain with syncope
Signs of cardiac herniation or strangulation
New onset arrhythmias or sudden cardiac arrest
references: Miller DL et al. Congenital absence of the pericardium: clinical and radiologic features. Radiographics. 2015.
MacDonald PS et al. Partial agenesis of the pericardium: diagnosis and management. Heart Lung Circ. 2018.
